common.disclaimer: This is a pre-feasibility estimate based on simplified assumptions. Actual carbon credit volumes will depend on formal project validation, species-specific growth models, and verified monitoring data.

landing.headline: Can your land earn carbon credits?
landing.subheadline: Answer a few questions about your plantation. In under 5 minutes, find out if your land qualifies for carbon credits under the Verra VM0047 methodology — and see an estimate of what it could be worth.
landing.noSignup: No sign-up needed. No uploads. Just answers.
landing.step1Desc: About your land, planting plans, and ownership. Takes under 5 minutes.
landing.step2Desc: We check your answers against Verra VM0047 criteria and tell you where you stand.
landing.step3Desc: Get an estimated range of carbon credits your land could generate over 20, 30, or 50 years.
landing.footer: CarbonFarm.io · Pre-feasibility screening for VM0047 ARR projects

section1.title: Basic Information
section1.subtitle: Tell us about your land and planned activity.
section1.landAreaHelp: Total contiguous area you plan to plant or restore.
section1.activityType: What type of activity are you planning?
section1.locationPlaceholder: e.g. Tamil Nadu, Chiang Mai, Mato Grosso
section1.locationHelp: Helps auto-detect your climate zone for carbon estimation.
section1.landParcelsHelp: Add each land parcel separately if you have multiple plots.

section2.title: Land History
section2.subtitle: These questions check whether your land meets the baseline eligibility requirements.
section2.methodologyRef: VM0047 §4.4.1 and §4.4.2 — the methodology requires that project land was not managed forest in the 10 years prior to the project start date.
section2.managedForest: Was this land a managed forest at any point in the last 10 years?
section2.managedForestHelp: A managed forest means land used for timber production, planned harvesting, or commercial forestry.
section2.timberHarvest: Has any timber been commercially harvested from this land in the last 10 years?
section2.timberHarvestHelp: This includes selective logging, clear-cutting, or any commercial removal of trees for sale.
section2.woodyBiomassRemoval: Has woody biomass (trees, shrubs) been deliberately cleared or removed in the last 10 years?
section2.woodyBiomassHelp: This includes clearing for agriculture, burning, or mechanical removal. Natural events (storms, fires) do not count.
section2.preExistingCover: What is the current tree canopy cover on this land?
section2.preExistingCoverHelp: VM0047 §6.2 requires that project land qualifies as non-forest at the start of the project. Land with more than 30% canopy cover is generally classified as existing forest.

section3.title: Land Tenure
section3.subtitle: Carbon credit projects need clear land rights for the full crediting period.
section3.ownershipType: What is your relationship to this land?
section3.owned: I own it (title deed or equivalent)
section3.leased: I have a long-term lease or concession
section3.documentedRights: Do you have documented proof of your land rights?
section3.documentedRightsHelp: This could be a title deed, lease agreement, government allocation letter, or community agreement.
section3.creditingPeriod: How long can you commit this land to a carbon project?
section3.creditingPeriodHelp: VM0047 requires a minimum of 20 years. Longer periods generate more credits.
section3.regulatorySurplus: Is planting trees on this land required by any law or regulation?
section3.regulatorySurplusHelp: For example, a government reforestation mandate, a court order, or a condition of your land permit. If the planting is voluntary, select No.
section3.regulatorySurplusRef: VM0047 §7.3.1 — the project activity must exceed what is required by law (regulatory surplus).
section3.regulatoryYes: Yes, I am required by law to plant here
section3.regulatoryNo: No, this is a voluntary decision

section4.title: Planting Design
section4.subtitle: These details help determine the monitoring approach and carbon estimation method.
section4.treeDensity: How many trees per hectare do you plan to plant?
section4.treeDensityHelp: VM0047 uses two monitoring approaches: census-based (≤50 trees/ha, direct planting only) counts every tree individually; area-based (>50 trees/ha or other activity types) uses sample plots and remote sensing.
section4.landUseContinuity: Will this land remain dedicated to the plantation for the full crediting period?
section4.landUseContinuityHelp: The land cannot be converted back to agriculture or other uses during the project.
section4.landUseContinuityNo: No, I may need the land for other uses

section5.title: Carbon Estimate Inputs
section5.subtitle: These help us estimate the carbon credit potential of your land.
section5.speciesType: What types of trees will you plant?
section5.speciesMultiHelp: Select all species you plan to plant. You can choose more than one.
section5.climateSuggested: Based on your location ({{location}}), we suggest: {{zone}}
section5.climateZone: What is the climate in your area?

results.title: Your Eligibility Result
results.eligibleDesc: Based on your answers, your land appears to meet the key requirements for a VM0047 ARR carbon credit project.
results.needsReviewDesc: Some aspects of your situation need clarification before we can confirm eligibility. This is common and usually resolvable.
results.ineligibleDesc: Based on your answers, your land does not currently meet the requirements for VM0047. See the details below.
results.censusBasedDesc: With {{density}} trees/ha (≤50/ha) and direct planting, individual planting units can be counted and measured directly per VM0047 §4.3.
results.areaBasedDesc: With {{density}} trees/ha, monitoring will use remote sensing and plot-based sampling to estimate biomass across the planted area.
results.priceDisclaimer: Based on current voluntary carbon market prices of $5–15 per tCO₂e. Actual prices vary by project quality, vintage, and buyer.
results.poolingExplainer: Your {{hectares}} ha would join a larger pool of nearby landowners. Carbon registries typically require projects of 100+ hectares. CarbonFarm handles the aggregation — grouping your land with others in your region into a single registered project. You retain ownership of your land and receive credits proportional to your contribution.
results.poolingNote: Pooling is managed by CarbonFarm at no upfront cost to you. Fees are deducted from issued credits.
results.methodologyLink: How we assess eligibility — VM0047 methodology reference

criteria.landHistoryPass: Your land has not been managed forest, had timber harvested, or had woody biomass removed in the last 10 years.
criteria.landHistoryFail: Your land has been used as managed forest, had timber harvested, or had woody biomass cleared in the last 10 years. This is a hard exclusion under VM0047 §4.4.1 and §4.4.2.
criteria.landHistoryFlag: You indicated uncertainty about your land history. This will need to be verified during project development.
criteria.preExistingCoverPass: Your land has less than 10% canopy cover, qualifying it as non-forest under VM0047 §6.2.
criteria.preExistingCoverFail: Your land has more than 30% canopy cover. Under VM0047 §6.2, this is likely classified as existing forest and does not qualify for an ARR project.
criteria.preExistingCoverFlag: Your canopy cover is in the 10–30% range or uncertain. This will need to be assessed using satellite imagery or a site visit to confirm non-forest status.
criteria.landTenurePass: You have documented land rights and can commit for the required crediting period.
criteria.landTenureFail: Land tenure could not be confirmed. VM0047 requires clear land rights for the full crediting period.
criteria.landTenureFlag: Your land rights situation needs further documentation. This is common and usually resolvable.
criteria.creditingPeriodPass: Your commitment of {{years}} years meets the VM0047 minimum of 20 years.
criteria.creditingPeriodFail: A commitment of less than 20 years does not meet VM0047 requirements. Consider whether a longer commitment is possible.
criteria.regulatorySurplusPass: Your planting activity is voluntary and not required by any law or regulation, meeting the regulatory surplus requirement under VM0047 §7.3.1.
criteria.regulatorySurplusFail: If planting is required by law, the project does not demonstrate regulatory surplus under VM0047 §7.3.1. Carbon credits can only be issued for activities that go beyond legal requirements.
criteria.regulatorySurplusFlag: It is unclear whether planting is legally required. This will need to be assessed during project development to confirm regulatory surplus.
criteria.plantingDesignPass: Your planting plan is consistent with VM0047 requirements.
criteria.plantingDesignFail: You indicated the land may not remain dedicated to the plantation. VM0047 requires land use continuity for the full crediting period.
criteria.plantingDesignFlag: Land use continuity is uncertain. This will need to be confirmed.

methodology.title: VM0047 Methodology Reference
methodology.subtitle: How each question in the eligibility screener maps to the Verra VM0047 v1.1 methodology for Afforestation, Reforestation, and Revegetation (ARR).
methodology.section1Desc: These questions establish the basic project parameters. VM0047 applies to Afforestation, Reforestation, and Revegetation (ARR) activities. The activity type determines which monitoring approach and quantification procedures apply (§4.3).
methodology.countryRef: Country — helps determine applicable climate zone, forest definition thresholds, and regulatory context.
methodology.landAreaRef: Land area — the project area in hectares. Small landholders (<100 ha) typically need to join a pooled project.
methodology.activityTypeRef: Activity type (§4.3) — VM0047 distinguishes between direct planting, direct seeding, and assisted natural regeneration. Census-based monitoring (§4.3.1) is only available for direct planting with ≤50 planting units per hectare.
methodology.section2Desc: VM0047 §4.4.1 and §4.4.2 define the applicability conditions. The project area must not have been cleared or degraded to create the ARR project opportunity. These are hard exclusion criteria.
methodology.managedForestRef: Managed forest (§4.4.1) — Land that was managed forest (including timber plantations) in the 10 years prior to the project start date is excluded. This prevents 'perverse incentives' where forest is cleared to create an ARR project.
methodology.timberHarvestRef: Timber harvest (§4.4.2) — Commercial timber harvesting in the last 10 years indicates the land was productive forest, which is an exclusion.
methodology.woodyBiomassRef: Woody biomass removal (§4.4.2) — Deliberate clearing of woody vegetation (for agriculture, development, etc.) in the last 10 years disqualifies the land. Natural disturbances (fire, storm) are not exclusions.
methodology.preExistingCoverRef: Pre-existing canopy cover (§6.2) — The project area must qualify as 'non-forest' at the project start date. The non-forest threshold varies by country (typically 10–30% canopy cover). Land above 30% cover is almost certainly classified as existing forest.
methodology.section3Desc: Clear land rights and regulatory surplus are fundamental requirements for any carbon credit project.
methodology.ownershipRef: Land tenure — The project proponent must have clear, documented rights to the land for the full crediting period. Owned land with title deeds is strongest; communal or unclear rights need additional documentation.
methodology.creditingPeriodRef: Crediting period (§3.2) — VM0047 requires a minimum crediting period of 20 years, with a maximum of 100 years. Longer periods generate more credits but require longer land commitment.
methodology.regulatorySurplusRef: Regulatory surplus (§7.3.1) — The project must go beyond what is required by law. If there is an existing legal obligation to plant trees on the land (e.g., a reforestation mandate), the activity is not additional and cannot generate carbon credits.
methodology.section4Desc: The planting density and land use commitment determine the monitoring approach and long-term viability of the carbon project.
methodology.treeDensityRef: Tree density (§4.3) — Determines whether census-based or area-based monitoring applies. Census-based (≤50 trees/ha, direct planting only) counts every individual tree. Area-based uses sample plots and remote sensing. Most commercial plantations (400–1,100 trees/ha) use area-based monitoring.
methodology.landUseContinuityRef: Land use continuity — The project area must remain dedicated to the ARR activity for the full crediting period. If the land is converted back to agriculture or other uses, the carbon stored in the trees is considered a reversal.
methodology.section5Desc: These inputs feed into a simplified allometric carbon model based on published data.
methodology.speciesRef: Species type — Different tree species have different growth rates (mean annual increment of biomass) and root-to-shoot ratios. Our estimates use published values from IPCC 2019 Refinement Guidelines Volume 4, Table 4.4 (root-to-shoot ratios) and IPCC 2006 Guidelines Table 4.12 (biomass growth rates in plantations).
methodology.climateZoneRef: Climate zone — Growth rates vary significantly by climate. Tropical zones have the highest biomass accumulation rates; arid zones have the lowest. The IPCC classifies forests by ecological zone for biomass estimation.
methodology.carbonMethodDesc: The estimate uses a simplified version of the VM0047 quantification approach:
methodology.carbonStep1: Above-ground biomass (AGB) growth is estimated using published mean annual increment (MAI) values from IPCC Table 4.12, specific to species and climate zone.
methodology.carbonStep2: Below-ground biomass (BGB) is calculated using the root-to-shoot ratio (R) from IPCC 2019 Refinement Guidelines, Table 4.4. BGB = AGB × R.
methodology.carbonStep3: Total biomass is converted to carbon using the IPCC default carbon fraction of 0.47 t C per t dry matter.
methodology.carbonStep4: Carbon is converted to CO₂ equivalent using the molecular weight ratio: CO₂e = C × 44/12.
methodology.carbonStep5: A ±30% uncertainty band is applied to produce a low-high range, reflecting the pre-feasibility nature of the estimate.
methodology.carbonStep6: Price range uses $5–15 per tCO₂e based on current voluntary carbon market pricing for ARR credits.
methodology.source1: Verra VM0047 v1.1 — Methodology for Afforestation, Reforestation, and Revegetation (May 2025)
methodology.source2: IPCC 2006 Guidelines for National GHG Inventories, Volume 4: AFOLU
methodology.source3: IPCC 2019 Refinement to the 2006 Guidelines, Volume 4, Chapter 4
methodology.source4: IPCC Wetlands Supplement (2013) — for mangrove root-to-shoot ratios
